findings.text: Global CR0 handler accepts a vcpu and a new guest value, refreshes shadow plus hardware images and arch copy, marks availability, then drives mode and interception updates.
Global CR4 handler accepts a vcpu and a new guest value, derives a hardware image with host forced bits and mode adjustments, updates shadow and arch copy and marks availability.
Global register cacher marks the requested register available then synchronizes vcpu state from hardware for stack pointer, instruction pointer, control registers and page directory pointers.
Global page directory pointer saver copies four hardware entries into vcpu arch storage and marks the collection available, expecting PAE paging to be active.

Global segment writer clears the segment cache then either updates the virtual 8086 shadow copy or writes base limit selector and rights to hardware, with special handling for task register and unrestricted guests.

Global segment reader returns descriptor fields either from the virtual 8086 shadow copy with selector refresh or from cached hardware base limit selector and rights with present derived from usability.

Global exception bitmap builder computes the intercept set from fixed faults, debug options, virtual 8086 state, page fault need, nested desires and extended feature state, then programs hardware filtering.

Guest control register updates form the entry that triggers transitions among real, protected, virtual 8086 and long modes based on protection enable, paging enable and long mode enable, delegating to dedicated helpers.
Segment field reads form lazy entries that consult a per field valid mask and fetch from hardware only on first use after invalidation, while writes invalidate the whole cache.

Hardware CR0 starts from guest value with always off bits removed, then forces always on bits that differ for unrestricted guests, adds write protect without extended paging, and keeps mode helpers out of the unrestricted path.

Hardware CR4 preserves host machine check enable, forces mode dependent always on sets for unrestricted, virtual 8086 and protected operation, and strips or adjusts user protection, address extension, page size, secure execution and protection keys under constrained paging.

When user mode protection is emulated, setting the guest request enables descriptor interception and hides the bit from hardware, while clearing restores direct behavior unless nested state retains interception.

With extended paging but without unrestricted execution, CR3 exiting stays enabled while paging is disabled and is cleared when paging is enabled outside nesting, while nested operation preserves the outer request merged with local clearing.

A change in paging enable refreshes CR4 handling to consume the new CR0, marks CR3 dirty on disable to enable transition, and ensures CR3 is cached before interception changes so hardware versus guest ownership stays coherent.

Base intercept set covers page fault, invalid opcode, machine check, debug and alignment check, with page fault removed when not needed, breakpoint added for combined guest debug options, general protection added for backdoor compatibility, and device not available added when dynamic extended state may be used.

Outside nesting the page fault filter is programmed locally with a narrow present versus reserved policy when extended paging intercepts faults, while nested operation merges the outer bitmap by union and leaves filter programming to the nested preparation path.

Control register caching merges only guest owned bits from hardware into arch copies, stack and instruction pointers copy directly, CR3 is skipped when load exiting indicates hardware holds host value, and page directory pointer caching delegates to extended paging saver.

While virtual 8086 is active, segment writes update shadow copies except task register selector which goes to hardware, and segment reads serve shadow copies with selector and base refresh when hardware selector diverged.

Long mode activation is tracked through the architectural extension flag, entering only on paging disable to enable edge and exiting on the reverse edge while that extension remains requested, with task state type corrected on entry.
Virtual machine container helper derives the enclosing extension structure from the generic virtual machine pointer for use in real mode setup.

A segment is described by base, limit, selector plus type, system, privilege, present, available, long, size, granularity and usability attributes, with access rights packed in a defined order and usability also implied by non present state.

Cached segment state holds per segment selector, base, limit and rights plus a bitmask indexed by segment times field count plus field, reset on writes and on first use after the segment collection becomes unavailable.

Protection enable drives a two state machine between real with virtual 8086 active and protected with it cleared, each direction saving current descriptors, flipping the flag, adjusting flags, task state, exception intercepts and descriptor conversions.

Paging enable under long mode request drives a long mode latch that is set on rising edge and cleared on falling edge by updating the extension active flag and fixing task register type for sixty four bit operation.
After CR0 update, an emulation required indicator is recomputed from current vcpu state and depends on the arch CR0 already holding the new value.
CR3 interception must not be optimized by comparing old paging state because that value can be stale relative to interception after nested entry, so current paging state alone decides the update.

Real and protected conversions behave differently under invalid guest emulation control, including selector tie to base, fixed limit and attribute normalization, plus a one time warning when a base is not paragraph aligned.

Unrestricted operation forces the accessed indication on segment types except local descriptor table to tolerate older userspace images, and real mode virtualization warns if attempted while nested because that combination is unsupported.

Intercept policy is expressed as a bit per exception vector with page fault filtering using present and reserved indications and a match requiring present, and virtual 8086 forces interception of all vectors.

Real mode entry installs a host supplied task base with a fixed size derived from a defined constant and a fixed access pattern, saves prior flags, then forces input privilege and virtual mode indications while preserving a defined owned subset on exit.
Guest debug control writes preserve host owned bits from the host shadow while accepting guest bits, and warn if the caller attempts to set host owned bits directly.

The set of CR0 bits that the first level guest may own starts from a possible set and excludes write protect when extended paging is disabled to allow shadow protection construction, with paging disabled optimization deliberately avoided to prevent circular dependence.
